#### 1. Crouzon syndrome-acanthosis nigricans syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.797)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:3690)

**Proposed mechanism:** FGFR3 gain-of-function variant (rs769904882) —DISRUPTS→ FGFR3 (HGNC:3690); FGFR3 (HGNC:3690) —INCREASES→ FGFR3 signaling pathway (WP:P200); FGFR3 signaling pathway (WP:P200) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:P005); MAPK signaling pathway (WP:P005) —INCREASES→ Abnormal cell proliferation (HP:0001377); Abnormal cell proliferation (HP:0001377) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial abnormalities (HP:0000278); Abnormal cell proliferation (HP:0001377) —LEADS_TO→ Acanthosis nigricans (HP:0001041). Gain-of-function mutations in FGFR3 lead to its constitutive activation, resulting in downstream signaling pathway activation (including MAPK). This aberrant signaling drives abnormal cell proliferation, manifesting as craniofacial abnormalities in Crouzon syndrome-acanthosis nigricans syndrome and contributing to the broader skeletal and skin phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a loss-of-function mutation in FGFR3 in patients diagnosed with either MONDO:0011274 or MONDO:0012833, or the absence of any FGFR3 variants in affected individuals. _(variant: rs769904882)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the overactive FGFR3 signaling pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for Muenke syndrome and Thanatophoric dysplasia type 1, or demonstration that one disease is caused by loss-of-function and the other by gain-of-function in FGFR3. _(variant: None)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared gain-of-function mechanism in FGFR3 for both Muenke syndrome and Thanatophoric dysplasia type 1 could lead to the development of targeted therapies aimed at inhibiting FGFR3 signaling, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.
